question: On 27 January 2024, the Italian Government, together with other Member States of the European Union, announced that it planned to suspend funding to the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA), effectively freezing work by the most important agency working in the Gaza Strip, even though the humanitarian conditions there are out of control.

By contrast, a number of Member States stressed the importance of continuing to support the agency’s work in assisting the population, which has been turned upside down by almost 4 months of war. In a recent statement, the Commission said that it would assess whether and how to continue funding the agency, clarifying that no further funding would be provided for UNRWA until the end of February.
Can the Commission answer the following questions: 1.
When is the next funding instalment for UNRWA expected and how much might it be?
Given the agency’s importance in providing aid and protection to innocent civilians, what humanitarian impact might suspending that funding have?
Given the deteriorating state of affairs, how will the Commission continue to support the people of Gaza by means of partner organisations in the coming months?
answer: The Commission has engaged with the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA)’s Commissioner-General and welcomed his commitment to tackle the serious issues at stake. The way forward and the measures and procedures for the disbursement of the Commission’s funding for UNRWA was agreed with the Agency on 1 and 6 March 2024.

The Commission requested to the Agency the following: agreement by UNRWA on the three workstreams (the screening of UNRWA staff; system audit; reinforcement of the Department of Internal Investigations and Ethics office) and the signature of the EU-UNRWA contribution agreement; declaration in writing by UNRWA that up-to-date, necessary and proportionate information on staff has been shared with the host countries and Israel and will be done on a quarterly basis; and the adoption by UNRWA of a concept note detailing how to strengthen the Department of Internal Oversight Services, including the establishment of a new neutrality investigation unit, and ethics office.

Following UNRWA’s positive engagement and fulfilment of these conditions, the Commission paid a first tranche of EUR 50 million out of the EUR 82 million foreseen for UNRWA for 2024 on 9 March. The second and third tranches of EUR 16 million respectively are subject to the implementation of the agreement with UNRWA and the Agency’s compliance with the agreed conditions and milestones.

On 1 March 2024, the Commission announced its decision to allocate an additional EUR 68 million in emergency support to the Palestinian population across the region to be implemented through international partners like the Red Cross and the Red Crescent. This support comes in addition to the support provided through UNRWA.
Furthermore, the Commission has allocated over EUR 290 million in humanitarian aid for Palestinians since the beginning of the conflict.

EU humanitarian aid to Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank continues unabated through partner organisations, and also includes a further contracting of EUR 16 million (separate from the payments described above) that UNRWA received from the Commission’s humanitarian aid budget for food, medical and non-food items, shelter, as well as education and psycho-social support to civilians in Gaza.

The EU recognises UNRWA’s vital role in the humanitarian response in Gaza, and that it also plays a crucial role for stability in the region (1). This was reiterated by the European Council on 21 March 2024, when EU leaders stressed that the services UNRWA provides in Gaza and across the region are essential (2).
